dataSource: Department of Atomic Energy, NPCIL, DAE Annual Report 2024-25, Ministry of Power
note: Pipeline capacities from official DAE press releases. Commissioning years are estimates based on government announcements. Actual dates may vary.

projects.name: 10 × PHWR-700 Fleet
projects.sites: Kaiga-5&6 (KA), Gorakhpur-3&4 (HR), Chutka-1&2 (MP), Mahi Banswara-1&2 (RJ), Bhimpur (MP)
projects.status: Site preparation + equipment ordering underway. Fleet mode construction — standardised design for faster build.
projects.keyMilestones: 2024: Cabinet approval for fleet mode. 2025-26: First pour concrete at Kaiga-5. 2028-31: Sequential commissioning.
projects.marketContext: India's flagship indigenous nuclear expansion programme. 10 units × 700 MW = 7 GW at ₹15 Cr/MW. Domestic manufacturing: L&T (vessels), Godrej (SGs), BHEL (turbines). Creates nuclear manufacturing ecosystem.

projects.name: Jaitapur-1 to 6 (MH)
projects.status: Longest-delayed Indian nuclear project. MoU signed 2008 but CLNDA right-of-recourse clause deterred EDF for years. 2023: India-France agreement to finalise engineering. Land acquired.
projects.keyMilestones: 2008: Indo-French nuclear deal. 2023: Engineering finalisation agreement. 2026-27: Expected construction start (delayed multiple times). 2032-35: First unit targeted.
projects.marketContext: Would be India's largest nuclear site (6 × 1650 MW EPR). EDF's EPR has troubled history (Flamanville 12 years late, Hinkley Point C 5 years late + £30B budget). CLNDA liability issue partially resolved but EDF still cautious. French government push for export.

projects.name: Kaiga-5&6
projects.sites: Kaiga, Uttara Kannada, Karnataka (adjacent to existing Kaiga-1,2,3,4)
projects.status: Part of 10 × PHWR-700 fleet. Site already has 4 operating units (880 MW). Excellent operational track record (world record at KGS-1). Infrastructure exists.
projects.keyMilestones: 2024: Included in fleet mode approval. 2025: Construction preparatory works. 2028: First concrete. 2032: Commissioning target.
projects.marketContext: Brownfield advantage — existing infrastructure, trained workforce, community acceptance (Kaiga has operated since 2000 without incident). Lowest execution risk in the PHWR-700 fleet.

projects.name: Bargi (MP)
projects.sites: Bargi, Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh (inland freshwater site near Bargi Dam)
projects.status: Greenfield site. Part of fleet mode. Environmental clearance process underway. Land acquisition in progress.
projects.keyMilestones: 2024: Site selection confirmed. 2025-26: Environmental clearance expected. 2027: Construction start. 2033: Target commissioning.
projects.marketContext: Central India location provides power to MP/CG/MH grid. Inland site (no coastal risk). Freshwater cooling from Bargi reservoir. First nuclear plant in Madhya Pradesh.

projects.name: Chutka (MP)
projects.sites: Chutka, Mandla district, Madhya Pradesh (near Narmada river)
projects.status: Greenfield site. Part of fleet mode. Some local opposition regarding displacement — R&R (Resettlement & Rehabilitation) being addressed.
projects.keyMilestones: 2024: Part of fleet approval. 2025-26: Land acquisition and R&R completion. 2027-28: Construction start. 2033: Target.
projects.marketContext: Second MP site (with Bargi). Narmada river provides cooling water. Social acceptance challenges from displacement — being managed through enhanced R&R package.

projects.name: Kudankulam-5&6
projects.sites: Kudankulam, Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu (adjacent to existing KKNPP VVER site)
projects.status: Brownfield site adjacent to Kudankulam VVER units. Indian PHWR-700 units alongside Russian VVER-1000 units at same complex. Infrastructure advantage.
projects.keyMilestones: 2024: Approved as part of fleet mode. 2026: Construction preparatory works. 2029: First concrete. 2033: Target commissioning.
projects.marketContext: Unique site with both Russian (VVER) and Indian (PHWR) reactor types. Demonstrates India's multi-technology strategy. Existing grid connection and cooling water infrastructure.

projects.name: Ruppur / NPCIL new sites
projects.sites: Multiple new greenfield sites under evaluation (UP, Rajasthan, Haryana additional units)
projects.status: Early stage — site evaluation and environmental studies. Part of long-term nuclear expansion vision beyond initial fleet mode.
projects.keyMilestones: 2025-27: Site finalisation. 2028-30: Clearances and construction start. 2033+: Commissioning.
projects.marketContext: Reserve pipeline beyond the confirmed 10-unit fleet. Ensures continuous construction activity for nuclear supply chain sustainability.

pipeline.label: Planned (Vision 2047)

projects.name: SMR Fleet (NPCIL)
projects.sites: To be determined — SMRs can be sited closer to load centres due to smaller exclusion zone
projects.status: R&D stage. BARC has completed AHWR-300 design. No construction timeline yet. Awaiting government decision on commercialisation pathway.
projects.keyMilestones: 2026-28: AHWR-300 design certification by AERB. 2030: Prototype construction decision. 2035-38: First SMR prototype. 2040+: Commercial fleet.
projects.marketContext: India's unique thorium-based SMR path. India holds 25% of world thorium reserves. If successful, provides energy security independent of uranium imports. No country has commercialised thorium SMR yet — India would be first.

projects.name: FBTR Commercial Fleet (BHAVINI)
projects.sites: Kalpakkam (TN) for initial units, then new sites
projects.status: Depends on PFBR operational success (commissioned 2026). If PFBR performs well, commercial FBR fleet will follow. 600 MWe FBR design under development.
projects.keyMilestones: 2026-28: PFBR operational data validation. 2029: 600 MWe FBR design approval. 2032: First commercial FBR construction start. 2038-40: First commercial FBR online.
projects.marketContext: Stage 2 of India's three-stage programme. FBRs breed more fuel than they consume — multiply India's nuclear fuel resource by 50-70×. Critical for long-term energy independence. Only Russia (BN-800) and India (PFBR) operate FBRs globally.

projects.name: Additional VVER Sites
projects.sites: New sites under India-Russia nuclear cooperation agreement (site selection underway)
projects.status: Subject to India-Russia bilateral agreement continuation. Upgraded from VVER-1000 to VVER-1200 (Gen III+ safety features). Geopolitical uncertainty due to Russia-West tensions.
projects.keyMilestones: Dependent on: (1) Kudankulam-3&4 successful completion, (2) India-Russia relations stability, (3) New site identification. Earliest: 2030 construction start.
projects.marketContext: Russia is India's primary nuclear technology partner (since 1988 agreement). VVER-1200 is Russia's latest export reactor. However, Western sanctions on Russia create uncertainty about long-term supply chain (though India has maintained bilateral relations).

projects.name: India–US AP1000 Sites
projects.turbineOEM: To be determined (likely BHEL under license)
projects.status: Most delayed foreign reactor project. India-US 123 Agreement (2008) enabled, but CLNDA right-of-recourse has blocked progress for 15+ years. Some movement in 2023-24 discussions but no concrete construction timeline.
projects.keyMilestones: 2008: India-US nuclear deal. 2016: Kovvada site allocated to Westinghouse. 2017-2024: Negotiations stalled over liability. 2024-25: Renewed discussions. Construction start: uncertain (2028 earliest).
projects.marketContext: AP1000 has had troubled history globally (Vogtle, USA: $30B overrun, 7 years late). Westinghouse went bankrupt in 2017 (now restructured). CLNDA right-of-recourse remains the showstopper — Westinghouse won't accept potential unlimited liability for equipment defects.

projects.name: Thorium Reactor Pilot
projects.status: Long-term R&D vision (Stage 3 of three-stage programme). Thorium → U-233 breeding demonstrated in lab. Commercial-scale deployment is 20+ years away.
projects.keyMilestones: Current: Lab-scale thorium irradiation in research reactors. 2030s: Thorium fuel testing in PFBR blanket. 2040s: AHWR prototype with thorium fuel. 2047: Commercial target (aspirational, aligned with India@2047 vision).
projects.marketContext: India's ultimate energy independence play. 11.93 million tonnes of thorium reserves (world's largest). If successful, provides essentially unlimited clean energy. However, no country has achieved commercial thorium power — India is furthest ahead but still decades away.

pipeline.note: Planned capacity from India's Nuclear Energy Mission for Viksit Bharat @2047. Government target: 100 GW nuclear by 2047.

newEntrants.title: New & Emerging Players — Private Sector Interest in Nuclear
newEntrants.note: India's Atomic Energy Act 1962 currently restricts nuclear power generation to government entities (NPCIL/BHAVINI). However, multiple private players are positioning for entry via: (1) supply chain participation, (2) lobbying for policy change, (3) SMR development partnerships, (4) nuclear fuel cycle services. The government's 100 GW by 2047 target will REQUIRE private participation — policy change is a matter of when, not if.

players.name: Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL)
players.interest: Mukesh Ambani has publicly expressed interest in nuclear energy (AGM 2024). Reliance's Faradion acquisition (sodium-ion batteries) shows energy technology ambition. RIL's engineering capability (Jamnagar refinery, largest globally) demonstrates ability to execute mega-projects.
players.timeline: No active nuclear project. Awaiting policy change to allow private generation. Could enter as developer if Atomic Energy Act is amended.
players.marketPosition: India's largest private company by market cap. If allowed, would bring massive capital + execution speed. Likely partner with foreign reactor OEM (Westinghouse/EDF/Rosatom).

players.name: Adani Group
players.interest: India's largest private power generator (17 GW thermal + 20 GW RE). Gautam Adani has indicated interest in nuclear during industry forums. Adani's infrastructure execution capability (ports, airports, power) relevant for nuclear construction.
players.timeline: No formal nuclear involvement. Would likely seek UMPP-style nuclear project if policy allows. 2030+ timeline realistic for first involvement.
players.marketPosition: Largest private power portfolio in India. Natural candidate if government opens nuclear to private sector. Could bid for reactor site development + O&M contracts.

players.name: Tata Group (Tata Power / Tata Advanced Systems)
players.interest: Tata Group has historical nuclear connection — TAPS at Tarapur is named 'Tata Atomic Power Station'. Tata Advanced Systems already supplies precision components to DAE/NPCIL. Tata Power could be a developer if policy opens.
players.timeline: Currently: supply chain participant (precision engineering). Future: potential developer role post-policy change.
players.marketPosition: Deep engineering heritage. Tata Consulting Engineers has nuclear design capability. Tata Steel supplies special grades for reactor components. Integrated group capability.

players.name: Larsen & Toubro (L&T)
players.interest: L&T Heavy Engineering (Hazira, Gujarat) is already the sole manufacturer of PHWR-700 reactor vessels, calandria, and end shields. L&T is THE critical private player in Indian nuclear — without L&T, no new PHWR can be built.
players.timeline: Currently manufacturing components for PHWR-700 fleet (7 GW pipeline). Multi-decade relationship with NPCIL. Order book visibility through 2035.
players.marketPosition: Monopoly position in reactor pressure vessel fabrication for Indian nuclear. No alternative domestic supplier exists. Global nuclear-grade fabrication certification (ASME N-stamp).

players.name: Godrej & Boyce
players.interest: Godrej Precision Engineering (Mumbai) manufactures steam generators for PHWR-700 reactors. Also supplies fuel handling systems and other reactor components. Critical to India's nuclear manufacturing ecosystem.
players.timeline: Ongoing orders for PHWR-700 fleet. Capacity expansion underway at Mumbai facility for larger order volumes.
players.marketPosition: Sole domestic supplier of nuclear steam generators. Precision manufacturing capability developed over 20+ years of NPCIL partnership.

players.name: JSW Group
players.interest: JSW Steel supplies special-grade steel plates for reactor containment structures. JSW Energy (13 GW portfolio) could be a nuclear developer if policy permits. Sajjan Jindal has spoken about nuclear energy's role in decarbonisation.
players.timeline: Currently: steel supply chain. Future: developer interest if Atomic Energy Act amended.
players.marketPosition: India's leading specialty steel producer. Nuclear-grade steel plate capability. JSW Energy has execution track record in power projects.

players.name: Walchandnagar Industries
players.interest: Manufactures reactor internals, pressure vessels, heat exchangers, and fuel handling systems for NPCIL. One of the oldest nuclear component suppliers in India (since 1970s).
players.timeline: Ongoing supply to NPCIL fleet. Orders linked to PHWR-700 programme.
players.marketPosition: Niche nuclear fabricator. BSE-listed. Smaller than L&T but specialised in nuclear-grade components.

players.name: MIDHANI (Mishra Dhatu Nigam)
players.interest: Produces zirconium alloys (fuel cladding), titanium, and special stainless steels for reactor internals. Also supplies alloys for PFBR (fast breeder reactor). Defence + nuclear dual-use metallurgy.
players.timeline: Ongoing supply. Capacity expansion for larger PHWR-700 fleet demand.
players.marketPosition: India's sole producer of zirconium alloy tubes for nuclear fuel cladding. Strategic national asset. GoI-owned (74% PSU).

players.name: NuScale Power (USA) — India Partnership
players.interest: NuScale's 77 MWe SMR design was first to receive NRC certification (2020). India-US civil nuclear cooperation could enable NuScale SMR deployment in India. However, NuScale cancelled its Idaho project (2023) due to cost escalation — commercial viability uncertain.
players.timeline: No active India project. Depends on: (1) India SMR regulatory framework, (2) CLNDA resolution for US companies, (3) NuScale commercial viability. 2035+ earliest.
players.marketPosition: Global SMR leader by regulatory progress. But cancelled only customer project. India would need policy/regulatory change + liability resolution before NuScale could enter.

players.name: Rolls-Royce SMR Ltd (UK)
players.interest: Rolls-Royce's 470 MWe SMR design targeting UK deployment by 2030s. India-UK trade discussions have included nuclear cooperation. Rolls-Royce has existing India presence (aerospace, marine). SMR scale suits India's distributed grid needs.
players.timeline: UK first deployment targeted 2030s. India deployment would follow 2035+ if bilateral agreement and regulatory framework established.
players.marketPosition: Strongest non-US Western SMR programme. UK government backed (£210M funding). India-UK post-Brexit trade deal could include nuclear cooperation chapter.
